headline: Tev reports long-horizon agent training gains from verified environments and dense progress rewards
summary: A 13 October preprint introduces Tev-Gym, a 1,170-environment synthetic training corpus with hidden latent-world specifications, strict task verifiers and staged progress scores. The authors use progress-potential reward shaping to train Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.8-27B, reporting higher scores than their base checkpoints on Agents’ Last Exam’s computing-and-math subset (ALE-CM). Tev-27B’s reported Pass@5 is 0.28 versus 0.17 for its base and equals the paper’s reported GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5 values under the listed harness. The authors also report transfer to selected Terminal-Bench computing-and-math subsets and a larger GLM-5.3-Flash model. These are author-reported results; this review did not independently reproduce them, and the project page lists code and data as forthcoming.
